AppShell.tagline: Frontier intelligence · Santa Catarina · Atlantic Forest

DataSummaryBar.tooltipSpecies: Lower-bound count of unique species names across all hexbins. The topSpecies list is capped at 10 per hexbin, so the true number is higher.
DataSummaryBar.tooltipSource: All occurrence records come from GBIF (Global Biodiversity Information Facility), aggregating data from museums, herbaria, iNaturalist, and research institutions worldwide.
DataSummaryBar.tooltipFrontier: Surveyed hexbins with at least one GBIF occurrence record, ranked by Frontier Score. The remaining hexbins are shown as unmapped territory on the map.

FrontierRanking.title: Top {limit} Frontier Locations
FrontierRanking.subtitle: Highest discovery potential in Santa Catarina
FrontierRanking.tooltipRanking: Ranked by Frontier Score among hexbins with at least one recorded observation. Higher score = more under-surveyed relative to habitat quality.

TaxonSelector.tooltipAll: Every organism recorded in GBIF for SC — plants, fungi, animals (vertebrates & invertebrates), bacteria, protozoa, and more. A plant appearing in the species list is expected behaviour.
TaxonSelector.tooltipVertebrates: Animals with a backbone only: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Amphibians, and Fish (Actinopterygii). Invertebrates and all non-animal kingdoms excluded.

HexDetail.scoreAnnotation: Frontier = survey gap × habitat quality. High habitat coverage with low observation density indicates discovery potential.
HexDetail.footer: DATA · GBIF  /  SCORES · ATLANTIC FOREST HABITAT + SURVEY GAP
HexDetail.tooltipRecords: A GBIF occurrence — one documented observation of one species at this location, from a researcher, institution, or citizen scientist (e.g. iNaturalist).
HexDetail.tooltipScoreBreakdown: Frontier Score = (1 − survey effort) × 0.53 + habitat quality × 0.47. Each component is normalised across all SC hexbins.
HexDetail.tooltipFrontierPotential: Combined score: how little this area has been surveyed plus how much Atlantic Forest habitat remains.
HexDetail.tooltipHabitatQuality: Estimated Atlantic Forest coverage fraction. Currently a uniform placeholder (0.5) — real values require downloading forest-cover data.
HexDetail.tooltipSurveyGap: How little this hexbin has been surveyed relative to all others in SC. 100% = never surveyed; 0% = most intensively surveyed.
HexDetail.tooltipTopSpecies: Most-recorded species across all taxa (plants, fungi, animals). Species group (kingdom/class) is not shown because it was not retained during data aggregation. Click any name to see full taxonomy on GBIF.

GapMap.tooltipCoverage: Each cell is an H3 hexagonal grid unit (~36 km²). Boundaries are algorithmic, not administrative — they don't align with municipalities or protected areas.

frontierScore.title: Frontier Score
frontierScore.intro: Each surveyed hexbin receives a Frontier Score combining how little it has been studied with how much suitable habitat remains.
frontierScore.weightsNote: Weights (0.53 / 0.47) favour the survey gap slightly because habitat data is currently a placeholder. Once real forest-cover data is loaded these weights should be re-evaluated.
frontierScore.caveat: This formula is model-deduced and has not been calibrated against field discovery rates.
tableRows: How intensively the hexbin has been surveyed relative to all others in SC. 0 = never surveyed; 1 = most surveyed.
Estimated fraction of the hexbin covered by Atlantic Forest. Currently a uniform placeholder (0.5).

surveyEffort.title: Survey Effort Score
surveyEffort.intro: Computed from four GBIF-derived metrics, each normalised 0–1 across all SC hexbins (min-max), then combined with fixed weights.
surveyEffort.normNote: Normalisation is relative to the active taxon filter — scores change when you switch between All Taxa and Vertebrates, because the reference population changes.
tableRows: Years between first and last record

habitatQuality.title: Habitat Quality
habitatQuality.intro: Intended to represent the fraction of each hexbin covered by Atlantic Forest — the biome with the highest endemic species richness in Santa Catarina.
habitatQuality.warning: ⚠ Current status: placeholder value of 0.5 assigned to every hexbin. Habitat quality does not currently differentiate frontier locations.

dataSource.title: Data Source
dataSource.introPost: (Global Biodiversity Information Facility), an open-access infrastructure that aggregates biodiversity data from institutions worldwide.
contributing: CRIA — Centro de Referência em Informação Ambiental
Digitised museum and herbarium specimens worldwide
excluded: Observations recorded after the data fetch date
Records without GPS coordinates (hasCoordinate=true filter applied)

taxaCoverage.title: Taxa Coverage
taxaCoverage.allIntro: All Taxa includes every organism with a GBIF record in SC — not just animals. This includes plants found by botanists and citizen naturalists, which is why plant species occasionally appear in the recorded species list.
taxaCoverage.vertebratesIntro: Vertebrates filters to animals with a backbone only, using these five GBIF taxonomic classes:
taxaTableRows: All animals — vertebrates AND invertebrates (insects, crustaceans, molluscs, worms…)
Vascular plants, mosses, ferns, flowering plants
taxaCoverage.groupsNote: Species group labels (e.g. "(Aves)") are not shown next to species names because kingdom/class information was not retained during the current data aggregation. Re-running the pipeline with extended fields would enable this.

geographicScope.title: Geographic Scope & Grid
geographicScope.intro: SC is divided using the H3 hexagonal grid at resolution 6, producing cells of approximately 36.1 km² each. Hexagons are preferred over squares because all neighbours are equidistant, reducing directional bias in spatial analysis.
geographicScope.bboxLabel: The grid covers this bounding box — not SC's administrative boundary:
geographicScope.edgeNote: Some hexbins near the edges may partially or fully fall outside SC proper (into Paraná to the north, Rio Grande do Sul to the south, or the Atlantic Ocean to the east). These edge hexbins will have zero or few records, which is expected and does not indicate a data error.

scientificCaveats.title: Scientific Caveats
scientificCaveats.intro: This tool is an exploratory research aid, not a peer-reviewed output. Use rankings to generate hypotheses about under-surveyed areas — not to draw conclusions. Cross-reference with local knowledge, published flora/fauna checklists, and protected area maps before planning expeditions.
tableRows: Model-deduced. Weights not calibrated against field discovery rates.
Placeholder (0.5 uniform). No real forest-cover data loaded.
Lower bound — topSpecies capped at 10 per hexbin.
Partial. Many valid observations are not in GBIF.
GBIF backbone taxonomy. May differ from other systems.
